title: The Main Event—Jesus is Born
paragraphs: Think of this as Jesus’s ancestry report. It proves he has the royal bloodline of King David and traces his roots all the way back to Abraham, the father of the Jewish faith.
§Era 1: The Founding Fathers

Abraham had Isaac, Isaac had Jacob, Jacob had Judah and his brothers, Judah had Perez and Zerah (the mother was Tamar), Perez had Hezron, Hezron had Aram, Aram had Amminadab, Amminadab had Nahshon, Nahshon had Salmon, Salmon had Boaz (his mother was Rahab), Boaz had Obed (Ruth was the mother), Obed had Jesse, Jesse had David — and David became king.
§Era 2: The Kings and the Collapse

David had Solomon (Uriah’s wife was the mother), Solomon had Rehoboam, Rehoboam had Abijah, Abijah had Asa, Asa had Jehoshaphat, Jehoshaphat had Joram, Joram had Uzziah, Uzziah had Jotham, Jotham had Ahaz, Ahaz had Hezekiah, Hezekiah had Manasseh, Manasseh had Amon, Amon had Josiah, Josiah had Jehoiachin and his brothers — and then the people were taken into the Babylonian exile.
§Era 3: The Waiting Game

When the Babylonian exile ended, Jeconiah had Shealtiel, Shealtiel had Zerubbabel, Zerubbabel had Abiud, Abiud had Eliakim, Eliakim had Azor, Azor had Zadok, Zadok had Achim, Achim had Eliud, Eliud had Eleazar, Eleazar had Matthan, Matthan had Jacob, Jacob had Joseph, Mary’s husband, the Mary who gave birth to Jesus, the Jesus who was called Christ.
There were fourteen generations from Abraham to David, another fourteen from David to the Babylonian exile, and yet another fourteen from the Babylonian exile to Christ.
Here is how the birth of Jesus Christ actually went down.
His mom, Mary, was engaged to be married to Joseph. Before they enjoyed their wedding night, Joseph discovered she was pregnant. (It was by the Holy Spirit — but he didn’t know that.)

Joseph was chagrined but noble. He obviously knew the baby wasn’t his, but he didn’t want to ruin Mary’s life or embarrass her in front of the whole town. So he determined to take care of things quietly so Mary would not be disgraced, planning to quietly break off the engagement.
But while he was stressing out and trying to figure this all out, he fell asleep. An angel of God showed up in his dream and said:

“Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to go ahead and marry Mary. The baby she is carrying is from the Holy Spirit. She is going to have a son, and you are going to name him Jesus (which means ‘God saves’), because he is going to save his people from their sins.”
This whole crazy situation was actually bringing the prophet's embryonic revelation to full term — backing up a promise God had made through him hundreds of years earlier. The prophet had said:
“Watch this: a virgin will get pregnant and have a baby boy. They will call him Immanuel” (which translates to “God is right here with us”).

When Joseph woke up from the dream, he didn’t hesitate. He stepped up and did exactly what the angel told him to do. He went through with the wedding and brought Mary home as his wife. However, he did not consummate the marriage until she had the baby.
When the baby was born, Joseph named him Jesus.

title: The Stargazers, the Psycho King, and the Escape
paragraphs: Jesus was born in the town of Bethlehem during the rule of King Herod. Not long after, a group of scholars (basically ancient astronomers) arrived in Jerusalem from the East. They started asking around, “Where is the newborn King of the Jews? We saw his star rising and came to pay our respects.”

When word of their inquiry got to Herod, he was terrified — and not Herod alone, but most of Jerusalem as well. Herod lost no time. He gathered all the high priests and religion scholars in the city together and demanded, “Where is the Messiah supposed to be born?”

They told him, “Bethlehem, Judah territory. The prophet Micah wrote it plainly: It’s you, Bethlehem, in Judah’s land, no longer bringing up the rear. From you will come the leader who will shepherd-rule my people, my Israel.”

Herod then arranged a secret meeting with the scholars from the East. Pretending to be as devout as they were, he got them to tell him exactly when the birth-announcement star appeared. Then he told them the prophecy about Bethlehem, and said, “Go find this child. Leave no stone unturned. As soon as you find him, send word and I’ll join you at once in your worship.”

Instructed by the king, they set off. Then the star appeared again — the same star they had seen in the eastern skies. It led them on until it hovered over the place of the child. They could hardly contain themselves: They were in the right place! They had arrived at the right time!
They entered the house and saw the child in the arms of Mary, his mother. Overcome, they kneeled and worshiped him. Then they opened their luggage and presented gifts: gold, frankincense, myrrh.
In a dream, they were warned not to report back to Herod. So they worked out another route, left the territory without being seen, and returned to their own country.
§The Midnight Road Trip

After the scholars left, an angel woke Joseph up in the middle of the night: “Get up! Take the baby and his mom and run to Egypt. Herod is hunting for this child to kill him. Stay there until I give you the all-clear.”
Joseph didn’t ask questions; he packed up and they fled under the cover of darkness.
They stayed in Egypt until Herod died — and that made the prophet’s words come true: “Out of Egypt I called my son.”

When Herod realized the scholars had tricked him, he flew into a rage. He commanded the murder of every little boy two years old and under who lived in Bethlehem and its surrounding hills. (He determined that age from information he’d gotten from the scholars.)

This was exactly what the prophet Jeremiah had said would happen: “A sound was heard in Ramah — crying and deep sadness. Rachel weeping for her children, refusing to be comforted, because her children are gone.”

Later, when Herod died, God’s angel appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt: “Up, take the child and his mother and return to Israel. All those out to murder the child are dead.” Joseph obeyed. He got up, took the child and his mother, and reentered Israel. When he heard, though, that Archelaus had succeeded his father, Herod, as king in Judea, he was afraid to go there. But then Joseph was directed in a dream to go to the hills of Galilee. On arrival, he settled in the village of Nazareth. This move was a fulfillment of the prophetic words, “He shall be called a Nazarene.”

title: Enter John the Baptist
paragraphs: While Jesus was living in the Galilean hills, John — called “the Baptizer” — was out in the desert country of Judea preaching. His message was simple and austere, like his desert surroundings: “Change your life. God’s kingdom is here.”
John and his message were authorized by Isaiah’s prophecy: Thunder in the desert! Prepare for God’s arrival! Make the road smooth and straight!

John was a wild guy. He wore a camel-hair habit tied at the waist by a leather strap, and he lived on a diet of locusts and wild field honey. People poured out of Jerusalem, Judea, and the Jordanian countryside to hear and see him in action. There at the Jordan River, everyone who came to confess their sins was baptized into a changed life.

But when John realized that a lot of Pharisees and Sadducees were showing up for a baptismal experience because it was becoming the popular thing to do, he exploded: “Brood of snakes! What do you think you’re doing slithering down here to the river? Do you think a little water on your snakeskins is going to make any difference? It’s your life that must change, not your skin! And don’t think you can pull rank by claiming Abraham as father. Being a descendant of Abraham is neither here nor there. Descendants of Abraham are a dime a dozen. What counts is your life. Is it green and flourishing? Because if it’s deadwood, it goes on the fire.”

“I’m baptizing you here in the river, turning your old life in for a kingdom life. The real action comes next: The main character in this drama — compared to him I’m a mere stagehand — will ignite the kingdom life within you, a fire within you, the Holy Spirit within you, changing you from the inside out. He’s going to clean house — make a clean sweep of your lives. He’ll place everything true in its proper place before God; everything false he’ll put out with the trash to be burned.”
Then Jesus appeared, arriving at the Jordan River from Galilee. He wanted John to baptize him. John objected, “I’m the one who needs to be baptized, not you!”
But Jesus insisted. “Do it. God’s work, putting things right all these centuries, is coming together right now in this baptism.” So John did it.

The moment Jesus came up out of the water, the sky split open. The Spirit of God came down like a dove and landed on him, and a booming voice from heaven said: “This is my Son. I love him, and I am incredibly proud of him.”

title: The Desert Showdown and the First Crew
paragraphs: Immediately after his baptism, the Spirit led Jesus deep into the wilderness to be tested by the devil. The devil was ready for it. Jesus went without food for forty days and forty nights. He was starving. Then the devil moved in: “Since you're really God's Son, say the word and turn these stones into loaves of bread.”
§Strike 1
Jesus shut him down with a quote from Deuteronomy: “People need more than bread to survive; they need the words of God.”
§Strike 2

For the second test the devil took him to the Holy City — the highest point of the Temple. “Since you're God's Son, jump,” the devil said, and he goaded Jesus by quoting Psalm 91: “He has placed you in the care of angels. They will catch you so that you won't so much as stub your toe on a stone.”
Jesus countered with another quote from Deuteronomy: “Don't you dare test the Lord your God.”
§Strike 3

For the third test, the devil took him to the peak of a huge mountain. He gestured expansively, pointing out all the earth's kingdoms and how glorious they all were. “They're yours — lock, stock, and barrel,” the devil said. “Just go down on your knees and worship me, and they're yours.”

Jesus' refusal was short and sharp: “Beat it, Satan!” Then he backed his rebuke with a third quote from Deuteronomy: “Worship the Lord your God, and only him. Serve him with absolute single-heartedness.”
The devil lost, packed up, and left. Angels came and took care of Jesus.

When Jesus heard that John had been arrested, he headed back to Galilee. He moved from his hometown Nazareth to the lakeside village of Capernaum, nestled at the base of the Zebulun and Naphtali hills. This move brought Isaiah's prophecy to life: “Land of Zebulun, land of Naphtali, road to the sea, over Jordan, Galilee, crossroads for the nations. People sitting out their lives in the dark saw a huge light; sitting in that dark, dark country of death, they watched the sun come up.” This Isaiah-prophesied revelation came to life in Galilee the moment Jesus started preaching. He picked up right where John left off: “Change your life. God's kingdom is here.”
§Building the Team

Walking along the beach of Lake Galilee, Jesus saw two brothers — Simon (later called Peter) and Andrew — fishing, throwing their nets into the lake. It was their regular work. Jesus said to them, “Come with me. I'll make a new kind of fisherman out of you. I'll show you how to catch men and women instead of perch and bass.” They didn't ask questions, but simply dropped their nets and followed.

A short distance down the beach, they came upon another pair of brothers — James and John, Zebedee's sons. These two were sitting in a boat with their father Zebedee, mending their fishnets. Jesus made them the same offer, and they were just as quick to follow, abandoning the boat and their father.

From there he went all over Galilee. He used synagogues as meeting places and taught people the truth of God. God's kingdom was his theme — that starting right now, they were under God's government, a good government! He also healed people of their diseases and the bad effects of their bad lives. Word got around the entire Roman province of Syria. People brought anyone with a sickness — whether mental, emotional, or physical. Jesus healed them, one and all. More and more people came, the momentum building. Besides people from Galilee, crowds came from the “Ten Towns” across the lake, others up from Jerusalem and Judea, still others from across the Jordan.

title: The Sermon on the Mount (The Rulebook Flip)
paragraphs: Seeing the massive crowd, Jesus hiked up a hill, and those who were apprenticed to him — the committed — climbed with him. Arriving at a quiet place, he sat down and taught his climbing companions. This is what he said: the greatest speech ever given, where Jesus flips the world's rulebook on how God's kingdom actually works.
§The Beatitudes
"You're blessed when you're at the end of your rope. With less of you, there is more of God and his rule."
"You're blessed when you feel you've lost what is most dear to you. Only then can you be embraced by the One most dear to you."
"You're blessed when you're content with just who you are—no more, no less. That's the moment you find yourselves proud owners of everything that can't be bought."
"You're blessed when you've worked up a good appetite for God. He's food and drink in the best meal you'll ever eat."
"You're blessed when you care. At the moment of being 'care-full,' you find yourselves cared for."
"You're blessed when you get your inside world—your mind and heart—put right. Then you can see God in the outside world."
"You're blessed when you can show people how to cooperate instead of compete or fight. That's when you discover who you really are, and your place in God's family."
"You're blessed when your commitment to God provokes persecution. The persecution drives you even deeper into God's kingdom."

"Not only that—count yourselves blessed every time people put you down or throw you out or speak lies about you to discredit me. What it means is that the truth is too close for comfort and they are uncomfortable. You can be glad when that happens—give a cheer, even!—for though they don't like it, I do! And all heaven applauds. You are in good company. My prophets and witnesses have always gotten into this kind of trouble."
§Salt and Light

"Let me tell you why you are here. You're here to be salt-seasoning that brings out the God-flavors of this earth. If you lose your saltiness, how will people taste godliness? You've lost your usefulness and will end up in the garbage."

"Here's another way to put it: You're here to be light, bringing out the God-colors in the world. God is not a secret to be kept. We're going public with this, as public as a city on a hill. If I make you light-bearers, you don't think I'm going to hide you under a bucket, do you? I'm putting you on a light stand. Now that I've put you there on a hilltop, on a light stand—shine! Keep open house; be generous with your lives. By opening up to others, you'll prompt people to open up with God, this generous Father in heaven."
§Completing God's Law

"Don't suppose for a minute that I have come to demolish the Scriptures—either God's Law or the Prophets. I'm not here to demolish but to complete. I am going to put it all together, pull it all together in a vast panorama. God's Law is more real and lasting than the stars in the sky and the ground at your feet. Long after stars burn out and earth wears out, God's Law will be alive and working."

"Trivialize even the smallest item in God's Law and you will only have trivialized yourself. But take it seriously, show the way for others, and you will find honor in the kingdom. Unless you do far better than the Pharisees in the matters of right living, you won't know the first thing about entering the kingdom."
§On Anger

"You're familiar with the command to the ancients, 'Do not murder.' I'm telling you that anyone who is so much as angry with a brother or sister is guilty of murder. Carelessly call a brother 'idiot!' and you just might find yourself hauled into court. Thoughtlessly yell 'stupid!' at a sister and you are on the brink of hellfire. The simple moral fact is that words kill."

"This is how I want you to conduct yourself in these matters. If you enter your place of worship and, about to make an offering, you suddenly remember a grudge a friend has against you, abandon your offering, leave immediately, go to this friend and make things right. Then and only then, come back and work things out with God."

Or say you're out on the street and an old enemy accosts you. Don't lose a minute. Make the first move; make things right with him. After all, if you leave the first move to him, knowing his track record, you're likely to end up in court, maybe even jail. If that happens, you won't get out without a stiff fine.
§On Lust

"You know the next commandment pretty well, too: 'Don't go to bed with another's spouse.' But don't think you've preserved your virtue simply by staying out of bed. Your heart can be corrupted by lust even quicker than your body. Those ogling looks you think nobody notices—they also corrupt."

"Let's not pretend this is easier than it really is. If you want to live a morally pure life, here's what you have to do: You have to blind your right eye the moment you catch it in a lustful leer. You have to choose to live one-eyed or else be dumped on a moral trash pile. And you have to chop off your right hand the moment you notice it raised threateningly. Better a bloody stump than your entire being discarded for good in the dump."
§On Divorce

"Remember the Scripture that says, 'Whoever divorces his wife, let him do it legally, giving her divorce papers and her legal rights'? Too many of you are using that as a cover for selfishness and whim, pretending to be righteous just because you are 'legal.' Please, no more pretending. If you divorce your wife, you're responsible for making her an adulteress (unless she has already made herself that by sexual promiscuity). And if you marry such a divorced adulteress, you're automatically an adulterer yourself. You can't use legal cover to mask a moral failure."
§On Oaths

"And don't say anything you don't mean. This counsel is embedded deep in our traditions. You only make things worse when you lay down a smoke screen of pious talk, saying, 'I'll pray for you,' and never doing it, or saying, 'God be with you,' and not meaning it. You don't make your words true by embellishing them with religious lace. In making your speech sound more religious, it becomes less true. Just say 'yes' and 'no.' When you manipulate words to get your own way, you go wrong."
§On Revenge

"Here's another old saying that deserves a second look: 'Eye for eye, tooth for tooth.' Is that going to get us anywhere? Here's what I propose: 'Don't hit back at all.' If someone strikes you, stand there and take it. If someone drags you into court and sues for the shirt off your back, giftwrap your best coat and make a present of it. And if someone takes unfair advantage of you, use the occasion to practice the servant life. No more tit-for-tat stuff. Live generously."
§On Enemies

"You're familiar with the old written law, 'Love your friend,' and its unwritten companion, 'Hate your enemy.' I'm challenging that. I'm telling you to love your enemies. Let them bring out the best in you, not the worst. When someone gives you a hard time, respond with the energies of prayer, for then you are working out of your true selves, your God-created selves."

"This is what God does. He gives his best—the sun to warm and the rain to nourish—to everyone, regardless: the good and bad, the nice and nasty. If all you do is love the lovable, do you expect a bonus? Anybody can do that. If you simply say hello to those who greet you, do you expect a medal? Any run-of-the-mill sinner does that."
"In a word, what I'm saying is, Grow up. You're kingdom subjects. Now live like it. Live out your God-created identity. Live generously and graciously toward others, the way God lives toward you."

title: How to Actually Live It Out (Sermon on the Mount, Part 2)
paragraphs: Okay, pay super close attention when you're trying to do good deeds. Make sure you're not just putting on a show for everyone. It might look impressive, like a great performance, but God, who totally created you, won't be clapping for that.

When you're helping someone out, don't try to make a big deal about it or draw attention to yourself. I bet you've seen people like this – I call them 'playactors.' They treat everything like a stage, whether it's a prayer meeting or just hanging out on a street corner, acting all caring only when people are watching, totally playing to the crowd.

Sure, they get some cheers and likes, but honestly, that's all they'll get. When you're helping someone, don't even think about how it'll look to others. Just do it – keep it chill, keep it quiet, don't make a scene. That's exactly how your God, who imagined you and loves you deeply, works behind the scenes to help you out.
§Praying Simply

And when you're talking to God, don't turn that into some dramatic performance either. All these people making a regular show out of their prayers, hoping for fifteen minutes of fame! Do you really think God is sitting there in a special box seat watching your act?

Here’s what I want you to do instead: Find a quiet, private spot so you won't even be tempted to put on a role-play in front of God. Just be yourself there, as simply and honestly as you possibly can.
The focus will shift from you to God, and you'll start to really feel his grace.

The world is full of so-called prayer warriors who actually know nothing about prayer. They're all about formulas, programs, and advice, trying to sell you techniques for how to get whatever you want from God. Don't fall for that nonsense.
This is your Father you're dealing with, and he knows way better than you do what you actually need. With a God like this, who loves you so much, you can pray super simply. Like this:

"Our Father in heaven, reveal who you really are. Set the world right; do what’s best – here on Earth, just like it is in heaven. Keep us alive with enough food to eat every day. Keep us forgiven by you and help us forgive others. Keep us safe from ourselves and from the Devil. You’re totally in charge! You can do anything you want! You’re amazing and beautiful! Yes. Yes. Yes."
In prayer, there’s a real connection between what God does and what you do. For example, you can't expect to get forgiveness from God without also forgiving other people.
If you refuse to do your part, you basically cut yourself off from what God wants to do for you.

When you choose to skip some meals or give up something you like to focus better on God (that's called an appetite-denying discipline or fasting), don't make a big deal out of it. You might become a minor celebrity for a bit, but it won’t make you a saint.

If you're 'training' inwardly (working on your spiritual life), just act normal outwardly. Go ahead and shampoo your hair, comb it, brush your teeth, wash your face. God doesn't need you to put on a show to get his attention.
He won't miss what you're doing; he'll totally reward you well.
§A Life Focused on God

Don’t hoard up treasures down here on Earth where moths can eat them, rust can corrode them, or – even worse! – burglars can break in and steal them. Instead, stockpile your treasures in heaven, where they’re totally safe from moths, rust, and burglars.
It's pretty obvious, right? The place where your treasure is, is the place you'll most want to be, and that's where you'll end up being.

Your eyes are like windows into your body. If you open your eyes wide with wonder and belief, your whole body fills up with light. But if you live with squinty eyes, full of greed and distrust, your body is like a musty, dark basement.
If you pull the blinds down on your windows (meaning you choose to live in darkness), what a super dark life you will have!

You seriously can't worship two gods at the same time. If you love one god, you'll end up hating the other. Adoring one will make you feel contempt for the other. You absolutely can't worship God and Money both.

If you decide to live for God, focusing your life on worshipping him, then it naturally follows that you won't fuss about what's on the table for dinner or whether your clothes in the closet are super trendy.

There's so much more to your life than the food you put in your stomach, and way more to your outer appearance than the clothes you wear. Look at the birds, they're free and not tied down to a job or worried about anything; God takes care of them.
And you matter way more to him than birds do.
Has anyone ever, by fussing in front of the mirror, gotten taller by even an inch? All this time and money wasted on fashion – do you really think it makes that much of a difference?

Instead of obsessing over fashion, go out into the fields and really look at the wildflowers. They never get ready or go shopping, but have you ever seen colors and designs quite like theirs? The ten best-dressed people in the country look shabby next to them.
If God pays so much attention to how beautiful wildflowers look – most of which are never even seen – don't you think he'll pay attention to you, be proud of you, and do his absolute best for you?

What I'm trying to get you to do here is to chill out, to not be so obsessed with getting stuff, so you can actually respond to all the amazing things God is giving you. People who don't know God and how he works stress out over these things, but you know both God and how he works.
Steep your life in God's reality, God's initiatives, and God's provisions. Don't worry about missing out. You'll find that all your everyday human concerns will totally be met.

Give your complete attention to what God is doing right now, and don't get all worked up about what may or may not happen tomorrow. God will help you deal with whatever hard things come up when the time actually comes.

title: Stop Playing Referee (Sermon on the Mount, Finale)
paragraphs: §A Simple Guide for Behavior

Alright, listen up: Don't be that person who constantly picks on others, jumping all over their failures or criticizing every little fault – unless you're cool with getting the exact same treatment back. Because, seriously, that critical vibe you're putting out? It's totally going to boomerang right back at you.

It's super easy to notice a tiny smudge on your friend's face but completely miss the ugly, judgmental look on your own. How can you even think about saying, "Hey, let me help you with that," when your own expression is all twisted up with contempt?

It's like you're putting on a whole show, acting all 'holier-than-thou' instead of just focusing on living your own part. Just wipe that nasty sneer off your own face first, and *then* maybe you'll actually be in a good place to genuinely offer a washcloth to your neighbor.

Also, don't be disrespectful or casual with things that are sacred, things that are about God. Joking around or being silly about them doesn't honor God at all. Don't try to reduce deep, holy mysteries to simple, catchy slogans. When you try too hard to make it 'relevant' or 'cute,' you might actually end up inviting disrespect for what's holy.
And when it comes to God, don't try to bargain with Him. Just be direct. Ask for what you need. This isn't some weird game of cat-and-mouse or hide-and-seek we're playing.

Think about it: If your kid asks for bread, would you trick them by giving them sawdust? If they ask for fish, would you scare them by putting a live snake on their plate? Even if you're not the best person ever, you wouldn't even think of doing something like that. You're at least decent to your own children.
So, don't you think the God who created you out of pure love will be even *better* and more generous than you are?

Here's a super simple, common-sense guide for how to act: Ask yourself what you want people to do for you, then be the one to take the initiative and do that for them. Seriously, if you add up everything in God's Law and what the Prophets taught, this is basically the main takeaway.
§Being and Doing

Don't go looking for shortcuts to God. The world is full of these 'surefire, easygoing' formulas for a successful life that promise you can do it in your spare time. Don't fall for that stuff, even though tons of people do.
The real path to life – to God! – is active and requires your full attention. It's not a walk in the park.

Be really careful of those fake preachers who always have a big smile, dripping with practiced sincerity. Chances are, they're just out to rip you off in some way or another. Don't be impressed by their charisma; look for their actual character. Who these preachers *are* is the main thing, not just what they say.
A genuine leader will never try to mess with your emotions or your wallet. These 'diseased trees' with their 'bad apples' are eventually going to be chopped down and burned, metaphorically speaking.
Just knowing the right password – like saying "Master, Master" – isn't going to get you anywhere with me. What's really required is serious obedience – actually *doing* what my Father wants.

I can picture it now: at the Final Judgment, thousands will strut up to me, saying, "Master, we preached your Message, we totally bashed demons, and our super-spiritual projects had everyone talking!" And do you know what I'm going to say?
"You totally missed the boat. All you did was use me to make yourselves look important. You don't impress me one bit. Get out of here."

These words I'm speaking to you aren't just little extras for your life, like home improvements to your standard of living. They are foundational words, words to build your whole life on. If you actually work these words into your life, you're like a smart carpenter who built his house on solid rock.
Rain poured down, the river flooded, a tornado hit – but nothing moved that house. It was fixed firmly to the rock.

But if you just use my words in Bible studies and don't actually put them into practice in your life, you're like a stupid carpenter who built his house on the sandy beach. When a storm rolled in and the waves came up, it just collapsed like a house of cards.
When Jesus finished speaking, the crowd totally burst into applause. They had never heard teaching like this before.
It was super clear that he was actually living everything he was saying – what a huge contrast to their usual religion teachers! This was seriously the best teaching they had ever heard.

title: Jesus Shows His Power
paragraphs: Jesus came down the mountain, and the crowd's cheers were still buzzing in his ears. Suddenly, a guy with leprosy showed up and fell to his knees in front of Jesus, begging, "Teacher, if you're willing, you can totally make me clean."

Jesus reached out and touched him, saying, "I totally want to. Be clean!" Just like that, all the signs of his leprosy vanished. Jesus then told him, "Look, don't go blabbing about this everywhere. Just quietly go show your healed body to the priest (that's how people confirmed a healing back then) and give thanks to God. Your life, now clean and grateful, will speak louder than any words about what I've done."
As Jesus walked into Capernaum, a Roman captain rushed up to him, looking super stressed. "Teacher," he said, "my servant is really sick. He can't even walk, and he's in terrible pain!"
Jesus replied, "Okay, I'll come over and heal him."

"Oh, no way," the captain quickly said. "I don't want to put you through all that trouble. Just give the order from right here, and my servant will be fine. I get how authority works, you know? I'm a guy who takes orders and gives them. I tell one soldier, 'Go,' and he goes; to another, 'Come,' and he comes; to my slave, 'Do this,' and he does it."

Jesus was seriously impressed, almost taken aback. He said, "Honestly, I haven't found this kind of simple trust anywhere in Israel, the very people who are supposed to know all about God and how he works. This man is like a preview of many outsiders who will soon be coming from every direction—streaming in from the east, pouring in from the west. They'll be chilling at God's kingdom banquet right alongside Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Then, those who grew up 'in the faith' but didn't actually have any faith will find themselves out in the cold, totally cut off from God's grace, wondering what even happened."
Then Jesus turned to the captain and said, "Go on. What you believed could happen has happened." And at that exact moment, his servant got completely well.

By this time, they were in front of Peter's house. When Jesus went inside, he found Peter's mother-in-law in bed, burning up with a fever. He simply touched her hand, and the fever was gone! The moment she was on her feet, she was already getting dinner ready for him.

That evening, tons of people who were tormented by demons were brought to him. He brought relief to those suffering internally and cured everyone who was sick physically. He was totally fulfilling what Isaiah had predicted a long time ago:
"He took our illnesses, he carried our diseases."
§Your Business Is Life, Not Death

When Jesus saw that the curious crowd was getting bigger by the minute, he told his disciples to get him across the lake to the other side. As they were leaving, a religion scholar (like a Bible expert) asked if he could tag along. "I'll go with you, no matter where," he said.

Jesus was pretty direct: "Are you ready to rough it? We're not staying in five-star hotels, you know. Foxes have dens, and birds have nests, but the Son of Man (that's Jesus referring to himself) doesn't even have a place to crash."
Another follower chimed in, "Teacher, please excuse me for a couple of days. I have to take care of my father's funeral first."
Jesus refused. "First things first. Your business is about life, not death. Follow me. Go after life!"
§Jesus Calms the Storm

Then he got into the boat, with his disciples right there with him. The next thing they knew, they were caught in a crazy severe storm. Waves were crashing over the boat—and Jesus was sound asleep through it all!
They woke him up, practically yelling, "Teacher, save us! We're totally going to drown!"

Jesus scolded them. "Why are you guys such scaredy-cats, such faint-hearts?" Then he stood up and told the wind to be silent and the sea to calm down: "Quiet!" The sea immediately became smooth as glass.
The men rubbed their eyes, completely astonished. "What is even going on here? The wind and the sea actually listen and obey his command!"
§The Madmen and the Pigs

They landed in the country of the Gadarenes and were immediately met by two madmen, who were victims of demons, coming out of the cemetery. These guys had terrorized the whole region for so long that no one even thought it was safe to walk down that road anymore.

Seeing Jesus, the madmen screamed out, "What do you want with us? You're the Son of God! You weren't supposed to show up here yet!" Off in the distance, a herd of pigs was grazing and rooting around. The evil spirits begged Jesus, "If you kick us out of these men, let us go live in the pigs."

Jesus said, "Go ahead, but get out of here!" Completely crazed, the pigs stampeded over a cliff into the sea and drowned. The swineherds (the guys who guarded the pigs) were scared to death and bolted.

They ran and told everyone back in town what had happened to the madmen and the pigs. Those who heard about it were furious about the drowned pigs. A mob formed and demanded that Jesus get out and not come back.

title: The Haters Show Up
paragraphs: §Who Needs a Doctor?

Jesus and his crew hopped back in the boat and sailed across the lake to his hometown. The second they got out, some guys showed up carrying a paralyzed man on a stretcher, setting him right in front of them. Jesus was totally impressed by their crazy faith and told the paralyzed guy, "Hang in there, son. Your sins are forgiven."
But some religious teachers (scholars) who were there started muttering, "Whoa, that's like, blasphemy!"

Jesus totally knew what they were thinking. He said, "Why are you all whispering and gossiping? Which is easier to say: 'Your sins are forgiven,' or 'Get up and walk'? Look, I'm just gonna make it super clear that I, the Son of Man, have the authority to do either, or even both..."

Then he looked at the paralyzed man and commanded, "Get up. Grab your mat and head home." And just like that, the guy did it! Everyone in the crowd was completely awestruck, amazed, and stoked that God had given Jesus this kind of power to do stuff like that.
As Jesus walked on, he spotted a guy named Matthew at his job, collecting taxes (which most people hated). Jesus simply said, "Come along with me." Matthew immediately got up and followed him.

Later, when Jesus was having dinner at Matthew's house with his close followers, a bunch of people with sketchy reputations — like tax collectors and other 'sinners' — showed up and joined them. When the Pharisees (a super religious group) saw Jesus hanging out with this crowd, they totally freaked out.
They started grilling Jesus's followers, "What kind of example is your Teacher setting, getting all cozy with crooks and outcasts?"

Jesus overheard them and shot back, "Who needs a doctor? Healthy people or sick people? Go figure out what this Scripture really means: 'I'm after mercy, not religion.' I'm here to invite the outsiders, not to coddle the insiders."
§Kingdom Come

A little later, John the Baptist's followers came up to Jesus and asked, "How come we and the Pharisees are super strict about disciplining our bodies and spirits by fasting (going without food), but your followers don't?"

Jesus told them, "When you're at a wedding celebration, you don't skimp on the cake and wine; you feast! You might need to chill out and be moderate later, but not right now. Nobody pours cold water on a fun bonfire. This is like Kingdom Come!"

He continued, "No one cuts up a fancy silk scarf to patch up old work clothes; you want fabrics that actually match. And you definitely don't put your new wine in old, cracked bottles, because they'll burst!"
§Just a Touch

Just as Jesus finished saying this, a local official showed up, bowed respectfully, and said, "My daughter just died. If you come and touch her, she will live." Jesus got up right away and went with him, his disciples trailing behind.

Right then, a woman who had been bleeding for twelve years managed to slip in behind him and lightly touched the hem of his robe. She was thinking to herself, "If I can just put a finger on his robe, I'll totally get well."
Jesus turned around and caught her in the act. Then he reassured her, "Courage, daughter. You took a risk with your faith, and now you're well." The woman was healed from that moment on.

By now, they had arrived at the town official's house. Jesus pushed his way through the gossips looking for a story and the neighbors bringing over casseroles. Jesus was direct: "Clear out! This girl isn't dead. She's just sleeping."

They basically told him he had no idea what he was talking about. But after Jesus got rid of the crowd, he went inside, took the girl's hand, and pulled her to her feet — alive! The news spread like wildfire throughout the entire region.
§Become What You Believe

As Jesus left the house, two blind men followed him, shouting, "Mercy, Son of David! Have mercy on us!" When Jesus got home, the blind men went in with him. Jesus asked them, "Do you really believe I can do this?"
They responded, "Why, yes, Master!"
He touched their eyes and said, "Become what you believe." And just like that, it happened. They could see! Then Jesus got super stern with them: "Don't let a single soul know how this happened."
But they were barely out the door before they started blabbing about it to everyone they met.

Right after that, as the blind men were leaving, some people brought a man to Jesus who couldn't speak because an evil spirit had struck him. As soon as Jesus cast the evil, tormenting spirit out, the man started talking as if he'd been talking his whole life.
The people were on their feet, applauding and saying, "There's never been anything like this in Israel!"
The Pharisees (religious leaders) were left sputtering, "Smoke and mirrors. It's nothing but smoke and mirrors. He's probably made a pact with the Devil."

Then Jesus went on a tour of all the towns and villages. He taught in their meeting places, shared the good news about God's kingdom, and healed their diseased bodies, fixing their bruised and hurting lives. When he looked out over the crowds, his heart just broke for them.

They were so confused and aimless, like sheep without a shepherd. "What a huge harvest!" he told his disciples. "But so few workers! Get on your knees and pray for more people to help with the harvest!"

title: The First Road Trip
paragraphs: No sooner had Jesus finished praying, than his prayer was answered! He called his twelve followers and sent them out into the 'ripe fields' (meaning, where people were ready to hear the message). He gave them some serious power: the ability to kick out evil spirits and to gently help people who were hurt or struggling.
§The Twelve Harvest Hands Sent Out
Here's the squad he sent out:

Simon (everyone called him Peter, which means "Rock"), Andrew (his brother), James (Zebedee's son), John (James's brother), Philip, Bartholomew, Thomas, Matthew (the tax collector), James (Alphaeus's son), Thaddaeus, Simon (the Canaanite), and Judas Iscariot (yeah, the one who eventually betrayed Jesus).
Jesus sent his twelve 'harvest hands' (his workers for God's kingdom) out with these instructions:

"Don't start by traveling to some super far-off place trying to convince strangers. And don't try to be all dramatic by taking on some big public enemy. Instead, go to the lost, confused people right here in your own neighborhood. Tell them that God's kingdom is happening now! Heal the sick. Bring people back from the dead. Touch those who are considered 'untouchable' (like people with leprosy or those outcast by society). Kick out the demons. You've been treated super generously, so live generously yourself."

"Don't think you need to put on a big fundraiser before you get started. You don't need a ton of fancy equipment. You ARE the equipment, and all you need to keep going is three meals a day. Travel light, seriously."
"When you roll into a town or village, don't insist on staying in some luxury hotel. Find a modest place with some modest people, and just be content there until you leave."

"When you knock on someone's door, be polite and friendly when you greet them. If they welcome you, keep your conversation gentle and kind. If they don't welcome you, just quietly leave. Don't make a scene or cause a fuss. Just shrug it off and move on."
"You can be sure that on Judgment Day, they'll be really sorry they missed out—but that's not your problem right now."

"Stay sharp, because this work I'm giving you is risky. You're going to be like sheep running through a pack of wolves, so don't draw extra attention to yourselves. Be as clever as a snake, but as harmless as a dove."

"Don't be naive. Some people will question your motives, and others will trash your reputation—all just because you believe in me. Don't freak out when they drag you in front of the authorities (like judges or governors). Without even knowing it, they've actually done you—and me—a favor, giving you a platform to preach the good news of the kingdom!"
"And don't stress about what you're going to say or how you'll say it. The right words will be there; your Father's Spirit will give you the words."

"When people figure out that you're presenting the living God, and not just some feel-good idol, they're going to turn on you. Even people in your own family might do it. It's pretty ironic: you're proclaiming so much love, but experiencing so much hate!"

"But don't quit. Don't give up. It'll all be totally worth it in the end. In those tough times, you're not going for success, you're going for survival. Be survivors! And don't worry, before you've run out of options, the Son of Man (that's me!) will have arrived."

"A student doesn't get a better desk than their teacher. A worker doesn't make more money than their boss. So be content—even happy—when you, my students, my harvest hands, get treated the same way I do."
"If they call me, the Master, 'Dungface', what do you think the workers can expect?"
"Don't let them intimidate you. Eventually, everything is going to be out in the open, and everyone will know how things really are. So don't hesitate to go public now, tell everyone the truth."
"Don't let the threats of bullies scare you into silence. There's nothing they can do to your soul, your deepest self. Save your fear for God, who holds your entire life—body and soul—in his hands."
§Forget About Yourself

"What's the price of a pet canary? Just some loose change, right? And God cares what happens to it even more than you do. He pays even greater attention to you, down to the last tiny detail—he's even numbered the hairs on your head!"
"So don't let all this bully talk intimidate you. You're worth way more than a million canaries."
"Stand up for me against what everyone else thinks, and I'll stand up for you before my Father in heaven. But if you chicken out and run away, do you really think I'll cover for you?"

"Don't think I've come to make life all cozy and comfortable. I've come to make a sharp cut—like a knife—between son and father, daughter and mother, bride and mother-in-law. I've come to cut through these cozy family arrangements and free you for God."
"Well-meaning family members can actually be your worst enemies. If you prefer your father or mother over me, you don't deserve me. If you prefer your son or daughter over me, you don't deserve me."

"If you don't go all the way with me, through thick and thin (good times and bad), you don't deserve me. If your first concern is always to look out for yourself, you'll never truly find yourself. But if you forget about yourself and focus on me, you'll find both yourself and me."
"We are really closely connected in this harvest work. Anyone who accepts what you do, accepts me, the One who sent you. Anyone who accepts what I do accepts my Father, who sent me."

"Accepting a messenger of God is just as good as being God's messenger yourself. Accepting someone's help is just as good as giving someone help. This is a huge job I've called you into, but don't get overwhelmed by it."

"It's best to start small. Give a cool cup of water to someone who's thirsty, for example. Even the smallest act of giving or receiving makes you a true apprentice (someone learning the ropes). You won't miss out on a thing."

title: Doubts, Whiners, and Real Rest
paragraphs: After Jesus finished giving His twelve disciples their instructions, He headed off to teach and preach in the towns around Galilee.

John the Baptist had been locked up in prison, and sitting in a dark cell was messing with his head. He sent his own crew to ask Jesus, "Are you really the Messiah we've been waiting for, or should we keep looking?"

Jesus told them, "Go back and tell John exactly what you're seeing: The blind see, the lame walk, Lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the wretched of the earth are learning that God is on their side. Is this what you were expecting? Then count yourselves most blessed!"
§After they left, Jesus talked to the crowd about John:

"When John's disciples left to report back, Jesus started talking to the crowd about John. 'What did you expect when you went out to see him in the wild? A weekend camper? Hardly. What then? A sheik in silk pajamas? Not in the wilderness — not by a long shot. What then? A prophet? That's right, a prophet! Probably the best prophet you'll ever hear. He is the prophet that Malachi announced when he wrote, "I'm sending my prophet ahead of you, to make the road smooth for you."'"

"Let me tell you what's going on here: no one in history surpasses John the Baptist; but in the kingdom he prepared you for, the lowliest person is ahead of him. For a long time now, people have tried to force their way into God's kingdom. But if you read the books of the Prophets and God's Law closely, you'll see it all building up to John — teaming up with him to prepare the way for the Messiah of the kingdom. Looked at that way, John is the 'Elijah' you've all been expecting to arrive and introduce the Messiah."
"Are you listening to me? Really listening?"

"How can I account for this generation? The people have been like spoiled children whining to their parents, 'We wanted to skip rope, and you were always too tired; we wanted to talk, but you were always too busy.' John came fasting, and they called him crazy. I came feasting, and they called me a boozer, a friend of the misfits. Opinion polls don't count for much, do they? The proof of the pudding is in the eating."
Then Jesus tore into the towns where he'd done most of his miracles, because they'd seen everything and just shrugged it off.

"Chorazin, you're doomed! Bethsaida, you're doomed too! If Tyre and Sidon had seen even half the miracles you guys saw, they'd have dropped to their knees ages ago. On judgment day, they'll get off way lighter than you. And Capernaum! You thought you were so awesome — you're going straight to hell. If Sodom had gotten the chances you got, it would still be standing today. On judgment day, even Sodom gets a lighter sentence than you."

Suddenly Jesus started praying out loud. "Father, Lord of heaven and earth — thank you! You hid your ways from the know-it-alls who act like they've got everything figured out, and you showed them plainly to regular, ordinary people. Yes, Father — this is exactly how you love to work."

Then Jesus turned back to the crowd, way more gentle this time. "My Father has handed everything over to me — what to do, what to say. It's a Father-and-Son thing, built on really knowing each other: nobody knows the Son the way the Father does, and nobody knows the Father the way the Son does. But I'm not keeping this to myself — anyone who's actually willing to listen, I'll walk you through all of it, step by step."
§The Ultimate Invitation
Jesus then dropped one of his most famous, comforting lines for anyone feeling burned out:

"Are you tired? Worn out? Exhausted from trying to follow all the religious rules perfectly? Come hang with me. I'll show you how to take a real rest. Walk with me and work with me—watch how I do it. Learn the unforced rhythms of grace. I won't lay anything heavy or ill-fitting on you. Keep company with me and you'll learn to live freely and lightly."

title: Rule-Breakers and the Unforgivable Sin
paragraphs: §In Charge of the Sabbath

One Saturday (the Sabbath, which was a day of rest and no work), Jesus and his crew were just chilling, walking through a field of ripe grain. His disciples were pretty hungry, so they started plucking off heads of grain and snacking on them. But then, some Pharisees (religious leaders who were super strict about rules) showed up and tattled to Jesus: "Hey! Your disciples are totally breaking the Sabbath rules!"

Jesus was like, "Seriously? Haven't you guys ever read about what King David and his buddies did when they were starving? They went right into the holy sanctuary (the sacred part of the Temple) and ate the special bread from the altar—bread that only priests were allowed to touch! And what about God's Law? Doesn't it say that priests working in the Temple break Sabbath rules constantly while doing their jobs, and nobody ever blames them for it?"

"Look, what's happening here is way bigger than just religious rules," Jesus continued. "If you actually understood what that Bible verse meant—'I prefer a flexible heart to an inflexible ritual' (meaning God cares more about mercy than strict ceremonies)—then you wouldn't be picking apart every little thing like this. The Son of Man (that's me) isn't just some guy who has to follow the Sabbath; I'm the one who's in charge of it."

After Jesus left that field, he went into their meeting place (a synagogue). There was a guy there with a hand that was all crippled up. The Pharisees asked Jesus, "Is it even allowed to heal someone on the Sabbath?" They were totally trying to trap him with that question.

He shot back, "Is there anyone here who, if their one and only lamb fell into a ditch, wouldn't pull it out, even if it was the Sabbath? Of course, you would! So, isn't being kind to people just as important, or even more important, than being kind to animals?"

Then he told the man, "Hold out your hand." The man held it out, and just like that, it was completely healed! The Pharisees were absolutely furious and stormed out, muttering about how they were going to get rid of Jesus.
§In Charge of Everything

Jesus knew they were out to get him, so he just moved on. A ton of people followed him, and he healed every single one of them. He also told them to keep it quiet, following the instructions laid out by the prophet Isaiah:

"Check out my chosen servant; I love him so much, he's my absolute delight. I've put my Spirit on him; he'll bring justice to all the nations. But he won't shout, won't raise his voice; there won't be any huge scenes in the streets. He won't stomp on anyone's feelings, won't push you into a corner. Before you know it, his justice will win; just hearing his name will be a sign of hope, even for people far away who don't believe."
§No Neutral Ground

Next, they brought a super unfortunate guy to Jesus—he was blind and deaf because he was possessed by a demon. Jesus totally healed him, giving him back his sight and hearing. The people who saw it were blown away, whispering, "Could this actually be the Son of David (the Messiah)?"
But the Pharisees, when they heard the news, were totally skeptical. "It's just black magic," they claimed. "He's pulling some devil trick out of his sleeve."

Jesus called them out on their slander. "Think about it," he said. "A judge who gives totally opposite verdicts on the same person just cancels himself out. A family that's always fighting falls apart. If Satan is kicking out Satan, then is there even any Satan left? If you're throwing devil mud at me, saying I'm a devil who kicks out devils, doesn't that same mud stick to your own exorcists (people who cast out demons)?"

"But if I'm sending these evil spirits packing by God's power, then God's kingdom is definitely here. How in the world do you think you can just walk into an awake, strong man's house in broad daylight and steal his stuff, unless you tie him up first? Tie him up, though, and then you can clean him out."
"This is war, guys, and there's no middle ground. If you're not on my side, you're the enemy; if you're not helping, you're just making things worse."

"There's nothing you do or say that can't be forgiven. But if you deliberately keep slandering God's Spirit, you're basically rejecting the very One who forgives. If you reject the Son of Man (me) because of some misunderstanding, the Holy Spirit can forgive you. But when you reject the Holy Spirit, you're like sawing off the branch you're sitting on, cutting yourself off by your own stubbornness from the One who forgives."
"If you grow a healthy tree, you'll get healthy fruit. If you grow a diseased tree, you'll get rotten, worm-eaten fruit. The fruit always tells you what kind of tree it is."

"You guys have minds like a snake pit! How do you expect anything you say to be worth anything when your minds are so full of nastiness? It's your heart, not a dictionary, that gives meaning to your words. A good person produces good actions and good words consistently. An evil person is like a blight (a disease) on the whole orchard."

"Let me tell you something: Every single one of those careless words is going to come back to haunt you. There will be a time when you have to account for them. Words are powerful; take them seriously. Words can be your salvation (your rescue). Words can also be your damnation (your destruction)."
§Jonah-Evidence
Later, a few religious scholars and Pharisees cornered him. "Teacher," they said, "we want to see your credentials. Give us some hard proof that God is behind all this. How about a miracle?"

Jesus replied, "You're looking for proof, but you're looking for the wrong kind. All you want is something to make you curious, to satisfy your craving for miracles. The only proof you're going to get is what looks like the absence of proof: Jonah-evidence. Just like Jonah was in the fish's belly for three days and nights, the Son of Man will be gone for three days and nights in a deep grave."

"On Judgment Day, the people of Nineveh will stand up and give evidence that will condemn this generation, because when Jonah preached to them, they totally changed their lives. Someone way greater than Jonah is here, and you're still arguing about 'proofs.' On Judgment Day, the Queen of Sheba will come forward and bring evidence that will condemn this generation, because she traveled from a far corner of the earth just to listen to wise Solomon. Wisdom far greater than Solomon's is right in front of you, and you're nitpicking about 'evidence.'"

"When a nasty, evil spirit is kicked out of someone, it wanders through the desert looking for a place to rest, some unsuspecting soul it can mess with. When it can't find anyone, it says, 'I'll just go back to my old place.' When it returns, it finds the person sparkling clean, but totally empty inside. So it runs out and gathers seven other spirits, even more evil than itself, and they all move in, throwing a huge party. That person ends up way worse off than if they'd never gotten cleaned up in the first place."

"That's exactly what this generation is like: You might think you've gotten rid of the junk in your lives and gotten ready for God, but you weren't welcoming to my kingdom message, and now all the devils are moving back in."
§Obedience Is Thicker than Blood

While he was still talking to the crowd, his mom and brothers showed up. They were outside trying to get a message to him. Someone told Jesus, "Your mother and brothers are out here, wanting to talk to you."

Jesus didn't answer directly, but instead asked, "Who do you think my mother and brothers are?" Then he stretched out his hand toward his disciples. "Look closely. These are my mother and brothers. Obedience is thicker than blood. The person who obeys my heavenly Father's will is my brother and sister and mother."

title: The Master Storyteller
paragraphs: §A Harvest Story

Around that time, Jesus left the house and chilled out on the beach. Super fast, a huge crowd showed up along the water, forcing him to hop into a boat. He used the boat like a stage, talking to everyone and telling them stories.

“Check this out: A farmer was planting seeds. As he tossed them, some landed on the road, and birds just swooped down and ate them. Others fell on rocky ground; they sprouted super fast, but because they couldn’t grow deep roots, they shriveled up just as quickly when the sun got hot.

Some seeds landed among weeds, and as they started to grow, the weeds totally choked them out. But then, some seeds fell on really good soil, and they grew into an amazing harvest, way more than the farmer could’ve ever imagined!”
“Are you actually listening? Like, REALLY paying attention?”
§Why Tell Stories?
Later, his followers came over and asked him, “Why do you always tell stories (parables)?”
He replied, “You guys have been given this awesome understanding of how God’s kingdom works. You get it. Not everyone has that gift, that insight; it hasn’t been given to them.

When someone is truly open to this, the understanding and insights just flow. But if they’re not ready, any chance of them getting it disappears super fast. That’s why I tell stories: to get people ready, to gently push them toward a cool awakening.
Right now, they could stare forever and not see it, listen until they’re exhausted and still not get it. I don’t want that old prophecy from Isaiah to happen again:

"Your ears are open but you don’t hear a thing.
Your eyes are awake but you don’t see a thing.
The people are so clueless!
They stick their fingers in their ears
so they won’t have to listen;
They screw their eyes shut
so they won’t have to look,
so they won’t have to deal with me face-to-face
and let me heal them."

“But you guys have God-blessed eyes—eyes that really see! And God-blessed ears—ears that truly hear! So many people, even prophets and super faithful folks from the past, would have given anything to see what you’re seeing and hear what you’re hearing, but they never got the chance.”
§The Meaning of the Harvest Story

“Now, let’s break down this story about the farmer planting seed. When someone hears about God’s kingdom but doesn’t really take it in, it just stays on the surface. Then, the Evil One comes along and snatches it right out of their heart. This is like the seed the farmer scattered on the road.

The seed that landed in the gravel? That’s the person who hears the message and gets super excited about it right away. But they don’t have a strong foundation (character), so when the initial excitement fades or things get tough, there’s nothing solid there to show for it.

The seed that fell among the weeds is the person who hears the kingdom news, but then worries and dreams about getting more stuff, wanting everything under the sun, totally choke out what they heard, and nothing good comes from it.
But the seed that landed on good earth? That’s the person who hears and truly takes in the Good News, and then they produce an amazing harvest, way more than anyone could ever imagine.”

He told another story. “God’s kingdom is like a farmer who planted really good seed in his field. But that night, while his workers were asleep, his enemy secretly sowed thistles (weeds) all through the wheat and then snuck away before sunrise.
When the first green sprouts came up and the grain started to form, the thistles showed up too.”
“The farmhands went to the farmer and asked, ‘Boss, that was clean seed you planted, right? So where did all these thistles come from?’
He answered, ‘Some enemy did this.’
The farmhands then asked, ‘Should we go and pull out the thistles?’

He said, ‘No, if you pull out the thistles, you’ll accidentally pull up the wheat too. Just let them grow together until harvest time. Then I’ll tell the harvesters to pull up the thistles first, tie them in bundles for the fire, and then gather the good wheat and put it in the barn.’”

Another story. “God’s kingdom is like an acorn that a farmer plants. It’s tiny compared to other seeds, but over the years, it grows into a massive oak tree, big enough for eagles to build their nests in it.”
Another story. “God’s kingdom is like yeast that a woman mixes into a huge batch of dough for dozens of loaves of barley bread—and then she just waits while the dough rises.”
All Jesus did that day was tell stories—it was a long afternoon of storytelling. His storytelling actually fulfilled the prophecy:
§The Curtain of History
Jesus sent the crowd away and went into the house. His followers came in and said, “Can you explain that story about the thistles in the field to us?”

So he explained. “The farmer who sows the pure seed is the Son of Man (Jesus himself). The field is the world, the pure seeds are the people who belong to God’s kingdom, the thistles are the people who belong to the Devil, and the enemy who sows them is the Devil.
The harvest is the end of time, the grand finale of history. And the harvest hands are angels.

“The picture of thistles being pulled up and burned is like a scene from the final act. The Son of Man will send his angels, they’ll remove all the ‘thistles’ (evil people) from his kingdom, throw them in the trash, and be done with them. They’re going to complain like crazy, but nobody is going to listen.
At the same time, people who lived good, holy lives will shine brightly and honor their Father’s kingdom. Are you listening to this? Really listening?

“God’s kingdom is like a treasure that’s been hidden in a field for years, and then someone just accidentally stumbles upon it. The finder is totally ecstatic—what an amazing discovery!—and immediately goes and sells everything he owns to get enough money to buy that field.

“Or, God’s kingdom is like a jewel merchant who’s on the hunt for the most beautiful, perfect pearls. When he finds one that’s absolutely flawless, he immediately sells everything else he has and buys it.

“Or, God’s kingdom is like a fishing net that’s thrown into the sea and catches all sorts of fish. When it’s full, they pull it onto the beach. The good fish are picked out and put in a tub; the ones that aren’t good to eat are just thrown away.

That’s exactly how it’s going to be when history wraps up. The angels will come and sort out the bad ‘fish’ and throw them in the garbage. There will be a lot of desperate complaining, but it won’t do any good.”
Jesus asked, “Are you starting to get a handle on all this?”
They answered, “Yes.”

He said, “Then you see how every student who’s really well-trained in God’s kingdom is like the owner of a general store who can grab anything you need, whether it’s something old or something brand new, exactly when you need it.”

When Jesus finished telling all these stories, he left there, went back to his hometown, and gave a talk in their meetinghouse (synagogue). He totally stole the show, impressing everyone. “We had no idea he was this good!” they said. “How did he get so wise, get such amazing abilities?”

But then, in the very next breath, they started tearing him down: “We’ve known him since he was a kid; he’s just the carpenter’s son. We know his mom, Mary. We know his brothers James and Joseph, Simon and Judas. All his sisters live here. Who does he think he is?” They got all bent out of shape.

But Jesus said, “A prophet is usually not appreciated in his own hometown and by his own family.” He didn’t do many miracles there because of their hostile indifference (they didn’t care and were against him).

title: A Gruesome Death and Walking on Water
paragraphs: Things get dark for a second. King Herod (the ruler of that area) heard what was being said about Jesus. He told his servants, "This has to be John the Baptist come back from the dead. That's why he's able to work miracles!"

Here's the backstory: Herod had arrested John, put him in chains, and sent him to prison to placate Herodias, his brother Philip's wife. John had provoked Herod by naming his relationship with Herodias "adultery." Herod wanted to kill him, but he was afraid because so many people revered John as a prophet of God.

But at his birthday celebration, he got his chance. Herodias's daughter danced for the guests. She swept Herod away. In his drunken enthusiasm, he promised her on oath anything she wanted. Already coached by her mother, she was ready: "Give me, served up on a platter, the head of John the Baptist." That sobered the king up fast. Unwilling to lose face with his guests, he did it—ordered John's head cut off and presented to the girl on a platter. She in turn gave it to her mother. Later, John's disciples got the body, gave it a reverent burial, and reported to Jesus.
§Feeding the 5,000

When Jesus got the news, he slipped away by boat to an out-of-the-way place by himself. But someone saw him and the word got around. Soon a lot of people from the nearby villages walked around the lake to where he was. When he saw them coming, he was overcome with compassion and healed their sick.
Toward evening the disciples approached him. "We're out in the country and it's getting late. Dismiss the people so they can go to the villages and get some supper."
But Jesus said, "There is no need to dismiss them. You give them supper."
"All we have are five loaves of bread and two fish," they said.

Jesus said, "Bring them here." Then he had the people sit on the grass. He took the five loaves and two fish, lifted his face to heaven in prayer, blessed, broke, and gave the bread to the disciples. The disciples then gave the food to the congregation. They all ate their fill. They gathered twelve baskets of leftovers. About five thousand were fed.
§Walking on Water

As soon as the meal was finished, he insisted that the disciples get in the boat and go on ahead to the other side while he dismissed the people. With the crowd dispersed, he climbed the mountain so he could be by himself and pray. He stayed there alone, late into the night.

Meanwhile, the boat was far out to sea when the wind came up against them and they were battered by the waves. At about four o'clock in the morning, Jesus came toward them walking on the water. They were scared to death. "A ghost!" they said, crying out in terror.
But Jesus was quick to comfort them. "Courage, it's me. Don't be afraid."
Peter, suddenly bold, said, "Master, if it's really you, call me to come to you on the water."
He said, "Come ahead."
Jumping out of the boat, Peter walked on the water to Jesus. But when he looked down at the waves churning beneath his feet, he lost his nerve and started to sink. He cried, "Master, save me!"
Jesus didn't hesitate. He reached down and grabbed his hand. Then he said, "Faint-heart, what got into you?"
The two of them climbed into the boat, and the wind died down. The disciples in the boat, having watched the whole thing, worshiped Jesus, saying, "This is it! You are God's Son for sure!"
§Healing at Gennesaret

On return, they beached the boat at Gennesaret. When the people got wind that he was back, they sent out word through the neighborhood and rounded up all the sick, who asked for permission to touch the edge of his coat. And whoever touched him was healed.
